obligation: G1 (benchmark) + G2 (teacher dataset) foundation for executable-operator synthesis (S027)
setup: torch 2.13 + MPS. Teacher function F(h) = down(silu(gate.h) * up.h) computed from bf16 gate/up/down (layer 31) on REAL MLP-input activations h = post_input_norm L31 [6827 tokens x 5120] (activations are IEEE fp16, weights bf16 -- a loader correction: fp16 read as bf16 gives NaN). Train = first 3413 tokens, HELD-OUT = last 3414. Quality = held-out relative-Frobenius output error; memorization guard = train-vs-held-out gap. RATE = active bytes/token (operator params x precision) vs q3 MLP (267M params x 0.40625 = 108.6 MB).

first_candidate_naive_gelu_bottleneck.note: naive 5120->d->5120 GELU, 800 Adam iters: ~0.44 held-out (vs q3 0.39), does NOT beat q3. Larger d got WORSE (0.44->0.54) => UNDERTRAINED / optimization-limited, NOT capacity-limited. This is a training-quality signal, not a refutation.

verdict: FOUNDATION VALIDATED (G1/G2 pipeline works): teacher F(h), q3 baseline, held-out benchmark, memorization guard, MPS training all functional. The naive first candidate is in the ballpark of q3 (0.44 vs 0.39) but undertrained. The real search -- narrower SwiGLU op, mixture-of-small-operators, structured nonlinear, recurrent-depth, with PROPER training -- is the Grok operator superwave. q3's 0.386 held-out is the bar every operator must beat at fewer active bytes.
next: SwiGLU-op probe (narrower intermediate, 3000-iter cosine) in flight; then fan out the Grok operator-family superwave (G3-G8) against this benchmark.
